impact: Shows AI server makers struggling to pass on soaring component costs, which hit Dell before its report; rising component costs are a sign of strong memory pricing, a plus for MU and DRAM suppliers.
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell about 16% on Tuesday after its fiscal Q4 report. Revenue rose 50% to $14.5 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.43 beat the $1.29 expected; it raised fiscal 2027 revenue growth guidance to 27% to 35%. But it guided adjusted operating margin to 14% to 15% from 15.1%, with the Cloud and AI unit at about 14% from 15.2%, as CFO Marie Myers said costs are rising faster than pricing. The drop was bigger than the 10.4% move options had priced in.
title: HPE falls 16% as AI server margin squeeze overshadows raised outlook
